3. General

Requirements

Y

3.1 General

3.1.1 The enclosures of the electrical apparatus, such as motor, switch and plug and socket, shall :onform to the requirements of IS : 2148-I 968 ` Specification for flameproof enclosure of electrical apparatus ( first revision ) `.

3.1.2

The moving .

parts of the fan shall not be directly

accessible

in normal working

condition.

3.1.3

The drill

shall be of robust construction

to withstand

the duty conditions

required

in mines.

3.1.4 The drill shall be designed for easy dismantling for maintenance of renewable components, various covers, such as motor end covers, switch covers, cable couplers, etc, provided for maintenance shall be designed such that their repeated dismantling shall not cause any damage likely to effect the flameproof characteristic of the drill.

3.2 Motor

3.2.1 The drill shall have a squirrel cage induction motor suitable 50Hz ac supply and shall conform to the requirements of IS : 325-1970 induction motors ( third revision ) `.

for operation `Specification

on 125V, 3ph for three phase

3.2.2 The motor shall be capable of giving power output of 1.1 kW, Max at declared speed of chuck f.or a period of 30 minutes continuously, without exceeding the temperature rise as specified ir Table 2. The current at this output shall not exceed 15A.

3.3.1 The switch for operating the motor shall be designed to be operated by a spring-loaded trigger placed in the handle of the machine and shall be able to break contact at the release of the trigger. The switch shall be dust-proof and shall be housed in a flameproof enclosure conforming to IS : 2148-1968. 3.3.2 The switch shall be a single pole switch for ac or dc applications.

3.4.1 .I The bolted type of cable couplers shall as far as possible, conform to IS : 6789-1972 ' Bolted flameproof cable couplers and adaptors ' and shall be designed to carry 15A at 125V. 3.4.1.2 The restrained type cable couplers and adaptors shall not be used.

3.4.1.3 In case of 5-point couplers and adaptors, the pin connected to pilot core shall make the contact with its tube, after and break before, the pins connected to the power cores of the cable make or break the contacts with the respective tubes. 3.4.2 earthing All external metallic parts of the drill shall be in effective electrical connection conductor through a mechanically secured and electrically efficient attachment. with the

3.4.3 Provision shall be made for firm gripping of the cable within socket assembly or in equally effective manner, in order to avoid undue tension in power terminals. The gripping arrangement shall withstand the weight of the drill when suspended and shall also be able to prevent entry of water in the plug and socket. 3.5 Chuck 3.5.1 The chuck dimensions shall be in accordance with Fig. 1. The driving slots shall be effectively shrouded and shall be able to engage effectively with drill rods conforming to IS : 7868-1975 ' Rotary drill rods for drilling principally in coal `.
Note-The chucks designed with dimensions other than those specified in Fig. 1 shall be deemed standard provided they satisfy all other relevant requirements specified herein. to comply with this

5. Tests 5.1 Tests as specified in Table 3 shall be conducted by the manufacturer on one drill out of a batch of 20 drills or part thereof for type tests. For routine test these tests shall be conducted on each drill. recorded on proforma as given in Appendix A.

Note-The

test results

shall be

5.1 .l For type tests, instruments of class 0.5 accuracy shall be used [see IS : 1248-1968 Direct actina electrical indicating instruments ( first revision 1 1 and for routine tests instruments of class I.5 accuracy shall be used ( see IS : 1248-1968 ). . 5.2 High Voltage Test

5.2.1 For switchThe test voltages of 500 V ( sinusoidal ac ) shall be applied for 5 seconds between the contacts of the switch and also between the pilot terminal of the switch and the frame. 5.2.1 .I Initially 50 percent of test voltages shall be applied which shall be increased gradually to its full rated test voltage in a period of not less than 10 seconds and shall be maintained for test period mentioned In 5.2.1.

5.3 Stalled Rotor Test -A balanced sinusoidal 125 V, 3 phase supply shall be applied to the stator of drill motor, rotor being locked. The stalled current shall not exceed 40 A. The motor shall be capable of carrying, without injury and after it has attained the temperature corresponding with its rating, the current of the stalled machine for a period of 15 seconds.

5.4 Operational Test for Switch -The tests as mentioned in 5,4.1 and 5.4.2 shall be carried out on one switch out of a batch of 1 000 switches or part thereof to check the mechanical and electrical endurance of the switch and shall be conducted at the supply frequency for which the drill is designed.

5.4.1 Switches designed to make and break the control circuit shall be tested for 10 000 operations, when carrying a current of 1 A at 50 V dc. The switch shall be able to withstand this test without mechanical or electrical breakdown.

5.4.2 Switches designed to make and break line current directly shall be tested for 5 000 operations when carrying three-phase current equal to that of the motor when stalled. The switch shall be able to withstand this test without suffering mechanical or electrical breakdown and without any flash occurring between terminals or between terminal and frame. 5.4.2.1 For the purpose of this test the voltage between phases, as measured at the terminal of ihe switch, shall be not less than 125 V on open circuit and not less than 100 V at the prescribed current, at a power factor equal to that of the motor when stalled. 4
